subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, if r₁ = 2, r₂ = 3, r₃ = 6 and r = 1, then prove that a = 3, b = 4 and c = 5.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Find Δ and s
steps.margin_note: One of the four marks. r is given here, so Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) can be used immediately — no reciprocal step needed.
lines: Given r₁ = 2, r₂ = 3, r₃ = 6 and r = 1

recall.must_convey: That Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) = 6 and s = Δ/r = 6.
accept: delta is root of one times two times three times six which is six and s is six
the area is six and the semi perimeter is also six
use the product of all four radii under the root
find the area and the semi perimeter

steps.why: With r given the chain is one step shorter than its twin. Recognising which links are already supplied is what keeps the working brief.
common_mistakes: Re-deriving r from the reciprocal formula unnecessarily.
steps.memory_tip: r is given here, so Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) can be used at once — no reciprocal step needed.

steps.label: Find each side from its ex-radius
steps.margin_note: Two marks — the bulk. Same pairing as the twin: r₁ with a, r₂ with b, r₃ with c.

recall.must_convey: That each ex-radius gives its own side, producing a = 3, b = 4, c = 5.
accept: each ex radius gives its side so a is three b is four and c is five
use r one equals delta over s minus a and so on
the sides come out as three four and five
a three, b four, c five vasthundi
find s minus a then a, and similarly for the others

steps.why: Each line is two steps: divide to get s − a, then subtract from s. Doing both in one line is where sign slips creep in.
common_mistakes: Reporting s − a as the side.
Pairing the wrong ex-radius with a side.
steps.memory_tip: The pairing is fixed: r₁ with a, r₂ with b, r₃ with c.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Check against 2s, and note the shape: 3, 4, 5 is the right-angled triangle, which is worth remarking on.

recall.must_convey: That the sides are a = 3, b = 4, c = 5 and the check a + b + c = 2s holds.
accept: the sides are three four and five and they add to twelve which is two s
a three b four c five, the check works
it is the three four five triangle
three four five, sum twelve equals two s
the answer is three four five

steps.why: 3-4-5 satisfies 3² + 4² = 5², so this is the right-angled triangle — a good sanity check that the arithmetic landed somewhere real.
common_mistakes: Giving the sides in the wrong order.
steps.memory_tip: Check against 2s, and note the shape — 3, 4, 5 is the right-angled triangle.
